mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 4% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decline does not correlate with subsequent earnings weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 7% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines by more than 100,000 jobs in the same month, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combined trigger does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% MoM signals a weakening demand side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 50 basis points in a month and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 3% YoY, it signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combined trigger does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 3% YoY signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or GDPC1 growth does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.
